messages:
pen-tester: quick heads-up from the engagement — i could infer KMS key alias names via a timing/response-size difference when probing /v1/keys?alias=<candidate>.
pen-tester: repro is small, used a low-priv API token and iterated aliases; some returned ~45ms, others ~120ms consistently. attaching short curl and timings.
pen-tester: ```
for a in $(cat candidates.txt); do 
  start=$(date +%s%3N); 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys?alias=$a"; 
  echo $(( $(date +%s%3N) - start ))
done
```
cory: thanks — can you drop the exact sample aliases & the timestamps you ran this at? also, did you see any content returned or just timing/302/403?
pen-tester: only timings and sometimes a 302 redirect to a key-detail URL for valid aliases; not returning materialized key material ofc. ran tests 2039123450-2039123465 UTC.
alicia: is auth required to trigger this? severity? :thinking_face:
pen-tester: yes auth required, but a low-priv user token works (no KMS GetKey permission). the timing appears before final KMS policy evaluation because of routing/alias resolution step.
ben: can we get CloudTrail + ingress LB logs for those timestamps? need to confirm server-side timing and rule eval path.
pen-tester: attaching a trimmed tcpdump + sample response headers (see gist link) — shows a HEAD/GET returning 302 vs 403 with ~70ms delta.
sec-bot: automated-classifier: potential info-disclosure via alias enumeration -> preliminary severity: HIGH (w/ customer-sensitive key naming). tags: pen-test, kms, timing-sidechannel.
devon: holding — if attacker needs an authenticated token and no key material is leaked, this might be an INFORMATION-DISCLOSURE issue, likely MEDIUM. need to confirm blow-up vector (can alias list be used to find PII?).
alicia: we need a canonical repro in staging with full debug logging (LB, routing, auth middleware, KMS proxy). assign @devon to run the repro in staging and gather CloudTrail + application logs. also request that infra keeps packet capture.
devon: on it. spinning up a staging env with the same routing rules. ETA ~2h. cc @ben for logs access.
cory: I'll open RED-SEC-301 in Jira and attach the pen report + artifact links. marking customer-impact potential: Dedicated and Private customers with predictable alias names.
pen-tester: retest done in a replay env i just provisioned — still able to distinguish alias existence with parallel requests. attached pcap and timings (replay-id 7f3a).
ben: received pcap, confirmed timing delta consistent across AZs. forwarding to forensics. adding a short-term SIEM rule to alert on >50ms variance on key lookup endpoints from same token over 30s.
alicia: proposed mitigation: make alias resolution constant-time and remove 302 redirect differences (always return same status + generic header). patch candidate: routing layer normalize-resolve v1.1.
devon: I can push a quick staging patch to normalize response path. will run the pener's repro after.
pen-tester: verified staging patch mitigates the signal for my current test harness. with normalization i can't reliably enumerate aliases within noise.
ben: good. we'll schedule a delayed full retest once patch is rolled to a canary fleet. added a follow-up alert to the runbook.
alicia: marking this thread as in-progress -> mitigation-applied. will re-evaluate severity after canary results. thanks everyone. :eyes:
